object_types.name: Student
object_types.definition: A person enrolled or eligible to enroll in course offerings at the university.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... Students have a student number.

object_types.definition: An academic course offered by the university, identified by a course code.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly... Each offering is of exactly one course

object_types.name: CourseCode

source_references.excerpt: Courses have a course code, like CS101.

object_types.name: CourseTitle
object_types.definition: The descriptive title of a course.

source_references.excerpt: Every course has a title and a credit value. The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.

object_types.name: CourseOffering
object_types.definition: A specific instance of a course taught in a specific semester.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings, not in courses directly. A course offering is a specific course offered in a specific semester.

object_types.name: OfferingId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a course offering.

source_references.excerpt: Offerings get an offering ID.

object_types.name: MaximumCapacity
object_types.definition: The maximum number of students that can enroll in a course offering.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering has a maximum capacity -- a cap on how many students can enroll.

object_types.name: Semester
object_types.definition: An academic period in which courses are offered, identified by a semester code.

source_references.excerpt: A course offering is a specific course offered in a specific semester... Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester.

object_types.name: SemesterCode

object_types.name: EndDate
object_types.definition: The date on which a semester ends.

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.

object_types.name: Instructor
object_types.definition: A person who teaches course offerings at the university.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor. An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

source_references.excerpt: Instructors have a staff ID

object_types.name: Grade

ambiguities.description: Is enrollment in a course offering optional or mandatory? The transcript states 'Students enroll in course offerings' but does not explicitly specify whether enrollment is mandatory for every student or whether students can exist without enrolling. Additionally, it is unclear whether every student must enroll in at least one course offering during each semester they are active.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings

ambiguities.description: Does every course have offerings, and does every semester have offerings? The transcript states that 'the same course can have multiple offerings' and 'each offering belongs to exactly one semester', but does not clarify whether every course must have at least one offering in some semester, or whether every semester must have offerings.

source_references.excerpt: So the same course can have multiple offerings?... Each offering is of exactly one course and belongs to exactly one semester.

ambiguities.description: Does every instructor teach at least one offering? The transcript states 'each offering is taught by exactly one instructor' and 'an instructor can teach several offerings', but does not clarify whether every instructor must teach at least one offering or whether an instructor can exist without teaching any offerings.

source_references.excerpt: Each offering is taught by exactly one instructor. An instructor can teach several offerings in the same semester.

ambiguities.description: Is the MaximumCapacity value constraint properly bounded? The transcript mentions credit values are 'usually between 1 and 6' but does not explicitly state whether capacities have similar constraints (e.g., must be positive, have a maximum). Should a value_constraint be inferred for MaximumCapacity to ensure positive integers?

source_references.excerpt: The credit value is a whole number, usually between 1 and 6.

ambiguities.description: Enrollment cardinality: Is the relationship between Student and CourseOffering through enrollment modeled correctly? Can a student enroll in multiple course offerings, and can a course offering have multiple enrolled students? The transcript confirms students enroll and the grade fact references 'each course offering they were enrolled in' (plural), suggesting many students per offering. However, the maximum capacity constraint on CourseOffering suggests a limit, but does not clarify if it is a hard constraint that prevents enrollment or just a tracking value.

source_references.excerpt: Students enroll in course offerings... Each offering has a maximum capacity... a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Grade timing and enrollment link: The 'Student receives Grade for CourseOffering' fact type assumes the student is enrolled in the offering. The constraint that 'a student gets at most one grade per offering' is clear, but the mandatory direction is ambiguous. Must every enrolled student receive a grade, or can enrollment exist without a grade? Conversely, can a grade be awarded without the student being enrolled (e.g., an incomplete or audit scenario)?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Value type granularity for dates: The transcript specifies 'start date' and 'end date' as semester properties but does not clarify the format or precision (e.g., date only, or datetime including time of day). Should these be modeled as 'date' or 'datetime'? Additionally, course offerings might have schedule times not mentioned in the transcript.

source_references.excerpt: A semester has a start date and an end date.
